gloss: to dig up; to unearth; to excavate

definitions.gloss: to dig up; to unearth; to excavate
definitions.explanation: Physically digging something out of the ground.

definitions.gloss: to discover; to find (something valuable or rare); to uncover
definitions.explanation: Figuratively finding something hidden or overlooked, such as a bargain, talent, or rare item.

examples.japanese: {畑|はたけ}から{石|いし}を{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I dug up stones from the field.

examples.japanese: {遺跡|いせき}から{土器|どき}が{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}された。
examples.english: Pottery was unearthed from the ruins.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}に{埋|う}まった{車|くるま}を{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}すのに{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: It took a long time to dig the car out of the snow.

examples.japanese: {古本屋|ふるほんや}で{珍|めずら}しい{本|ほん}を{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I found a rare book at a secondhand bookstore.

examples.japanese: フリーマーケットで{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの}を{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: I found a bargain at the flea market.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{才能|さいのう}を{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}すのがスカウトの{仕事|しごと}だ。
examples.english: Discovering new talent is a scout's job.

notes:
A compound verb combining {掘|ほ}る (to dig) and {出|だ}す (to take out). The literal sense refers to physically digging something from the ground. The figurative sense of discovering something valuable is very common, especially in the compound {掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの} (a great find, a bargain).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの}: a lucky find, a bargain
- {才能|さいのう}を{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}す: to discover talent
- {遺跡|いせき}から{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}す: to excavate from ruins

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive. The intransitive counterpart would use {出|で}る: {掘|ほ}り{出|だ}す (to dig out) vs. simply {出|で}てくる (to come out).
